payload.stem: At a certain temperature the reaction A(g) ⇌ B(g) + C(g) has Kc = 6.4×10⁻⁹. A closed container starts with [A] = 0.1 M and no B or C. Which statement gives the equilibrium concentration of B and a correct reason the simplification used to find it is valid?

options.text: [B] ≈ 5.1×10⁻⁵ M, found from the same simplified expression after multiplying x by 2 although B has a coefficient of 1, which is valid because Kc is so small.
options.why: Mishandles the coefficient when converting the change x into the equilibrium concentration.

options.text: [B] ≈ 8.0×10⁻⁵ M, found by taking the square root of Kc alone, which is valid because Kc is so small that the initial concentration does not matter.
options.why: Drops the initial concentration from the expression, treating the square root of Kc as the answer.

options.text: [B] ≈ 2.5×10⁻⁵ M, found from Kc = x²/(0.1 − x) ≈ x²/0.1, which is valid because x is only about 0.025% of the initial concentration.
options.why: With x as the change, Kc = x²/(0.1 − x) ≈ x²/0.1 gives x ≈ 2.5×10⁻⁵ M (the quadratic gives 2.5×10⁻⁵ M, the same to two figures), so [B] = x = 2.5×10⁻⁵ M; x is 0.0253% of 0.1 M, below the 5% rule, so dropping x from the subtraction is justified.

options.text: [B] ≈ 6.4×10⁻⁹ M, because a very small Kc means the equilibrium concentration of the product is approximately equal to Kc itself.
options.why: Treats the numerical value of Kc as a concentration instead of a ratio of concentrations.

With x as the change, Kc = x²/(0.25 − x) ≈ x²/0.25 gives x ≈ 6.3×10⁻⁵ M (the quadratic gives 6.3×10⁻⁵ M, the same to two figures), so [B] = x = 6.3×10⁻⁵ M; x is 0.0253% of 0.25 M, below the 5% rule, so dropping x from the subtraction is justified.
[B] ≈ 1.3×10⁻⁴ M, found by taking the square root of Kc alone, which is valid because Kc is so small that the initial concentration does not matter. is incorrect: Drops the initial concentration from the expression, treating the square root of Kc as the answer.
[B] ≈ 1.3×10⁻⁴ M, found from the same simplified expression after multiplying x by 2 although B has a coefficient of 1, which is valid because Kc is so small. is incorrect: Mishandles the coefficient when converting the change x into the equilibrium concentration.
[B] ≈ 1.6×10⁻⁸ M, because a very small Kc means the equilibrium concentration of the product is approximately equal to Kc itself. is incorrect: Treats the numerical value of Kc as a concentration instead of a ratio of concentrations.

difficulty.label: exam_prep
difficulty.rationale: Single-equilibrium ICE setup with the small-x approximation, a square-root solve, and a percent-ionization-style validity check, all within 7.7 scope. The answer options pair a numeric result with its justification, which adds one reasoning step. Distractors reflect plausible errors: ignoring the initial concentration, doubling x, and equating [B] with Kc. Arithmetic is short and the wording is clear, so the difficulty is conceptual rather than coming from unfair sources.
